source.snippet: When data collection for an account stops working, the user isn't told. Users find out themselves, often weeks later, or never. Recent example: two accounts on the same instance hadn't received new stats for 42 days before one user emailed us.

problem_statement: Small SaaS products lack a reliable mechanism to detect and proactively notify users when their background data-collection pipelines silently fail, leading to users discovering data gaps days or weeks later — eroding trust and triggering churn.
target_segment: Solo operators and small teams running SaaS analytics or data-aggregation products where scheduled background jobs collect third-party data on behalf of users.
notes: Commercial context: this is a live SaaS product (Analytodon, a Mastodon analytics tool) with real paying or active users. The issue describes a 42-day silent failure that the operator only discovered when a user emailed in. The pain is real and recurring. A lightweight 'data freshness watchdog' service — one that monitors last-updated timestamps per user account and fires notifications when a threshold is exceeded — could be sold to small SaaS operators. Willingness-to-pay is implied by operators' need to retain subscribers and avoid support escalations. Single source but concrete operational failure with named consequences.
